nodes.name: Interfacial Thermal Distillation
nodes.procedure: Interfacial thermal evaporator (capillary wick) attached to PV panel backside enables passive seawater supply via capillary effect. Waste heat from PV panel (40.9°C) drives evaporation. Unidirectional flow via siphon effect (h=6 cm elevation difference between inlet/outlet reservoirs) prevents salt accumulation (steady-state outlet salinity 5 wt% for 3.5 wt% seawater, 15 wt% for 10.5 wt% brine). Vapor condenses on L-shaped stainless steel BP (5 cm slots, 1 mm width). Distilled water flows through slots to wet GDL. Air gap (1.5 cm) via polycarbonate spacer separates evaporator from electrolyzer.

unit_operations.name: Capillary Seawater Supply
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: The evaporator has a wicking structure, enabling a passive supply of seawater due to the capillary effect.

unit_operations.name: Interfacial Evaporation
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: Waste heat is transferred from the PV panel to the evaporator, driving the seawater distillation.

unit_operations.name: Siphon-Driven Flow
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: The unidirectional flow is driven by the siphon effect, where no pumping power is required.

unit_operations.name: Vapor Condensation
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: Vapor condensation occurred on the BP. Distilled water can directly flow through the slots and wet the GDL.

nodes.source_text: Fig. 1b shows the working principle... An interfacial thermal evaporator is attached to the backside of the PV panel (Fig. 2a).

nodes.name: Coupled PV-PEM Electrolysis
nodes.procedure: PEM electrolyzer (25 cm² active area) with Ti GDLs (5×5 cm²), Pt-based cathode catalyst, Ir-based anode catalyst. 4 Si solar cells in series provide ~2.07 V, ~417 mA at I-V intersection (near PV MPP). Distilled water condenses directly on anode-side L-shaped SS BP (serves as condenser/heat sink), flows through parallel slots to wet GDL. Latent heat elevates PEM temperature to 31°C. Cathode produces H₂ gas collected via water displacement. STH efficiency 12.6% (HHV basis).

unit_operations.name: PV-Electrolyzer Coupling
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: The coupling between the PV panel and PEM electrolyzer resulted in an intersection point at ~2.07 V and ~417 mA.

unit_operations.name: Condensation Heating
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: Latent heat released during condensation is transported to the electrolyzer, which elevates the temperature.

unit_operations.name: PEM Water Splitting
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: With electricity produced by the PV panel, hydrogen is generated from the cathode of the PEM electrolyzer.
